newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese inflation slows to 30-year lows.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese inflation slows to 30-year lows.

text.p: Portugal's inflation slowed sharply to 1.8 percent year-on-year in April, a rate not seen since the 1960s, the National Statistics Institute said on Tuesday.
The rate compared with 2.5 percent in March.

The precipitous drop had been widely predicted for statistical reasons because in the same month last year, the consumer price index (CPI) was driven higher by rising meat prices provoked by Europe's mad-cow scare.
The month-on-month rise in April was 0.2 percent against 0.9 percent in April 1996 when prices rose two percent year-on-year.
"The rate confirmed the best expectations," said one bond market trader.
The April figures took the moving 12-month average, the government's benchmark rate, to 3.1 percent, down from 3.2 percent in March and 3.4 percent a year ago.
The government is committed to getting the moving average down to 2.25-2.5 percent by the end of the year as part of its drive to qualify Portugal for the European Union's single currency.
